title: If Medicare calls demanding your card number
prompt: A caller says they are from Medicare and your benefits will be cancelled unless you give your card number. Put these steps in order:
steps: Look up the official Medicare phone number on your red, white, and blue card or at Medicare.gov.
Hang up immediately. Government agencies do not call out of the blue to threaten benefits.
Call official Medicare directly if you have any genuine concerns about your account.
Report the scam phone number to the Federal Trade Commission.
whyFirstStepMatters: Hanging up prevents you from accidentally revealing sensitive numbers under pressure. Government workers will never threaten you or demand immediate payment over the phone.
explanation: Medicare and Social Security communicate primarily through official mail. They never call to threaten suspension of benefits or demand payment over the phone.
takeaways: Medicare never calls unexpectedly demanding card numbers.
Hang up and call the number on your official card.

title: Text threatening immediate IRS arrest warrant

segments.text: Your tax file shows an unpaid delinquent assessment of $1,840.

flag.reason: The IRS contacts taxpayers by official postal mail, never by unsolicited text messages.

segments.text: A federal arrest warrant has been signed and local deputies will visit your residence within 2 hours.

flag.reason: The IRS cannot and will not dispatch local police to arrest citizens over tax disputes.

segments.text: To cancel the warrant, settle immediately at irs-tax-settlement-gov.com or call our field desk.

flag.reason: All authentic IRS websites end strictly in .gov, never in .com.

explanation: The IRS never demands immediate payment over the phone or text, and never threatens immediate arrest by local police. All legitimate IRS notices arrive through the U.S. Mail.
takeaways: The IRS sends letters by postal mail, never text messages.
Real government agencies never threaten immediate arrest over text.
